Split

Stratified split: 70 / 15 / 15

  • Problem: a random split could leave too few rare-class images in the test set
  • Rule: each image goes to the pile of its rarest class
  • 4 banana peels + 1 newspaper → paper pile
  • Each pile shuffled (seed 42) and cut 70/15/15
  • Result: similar class shares in train, val and test

Model training & evaluation

Test set (1,574 images, used once)

PRmAP50mAP50-95
Validation0.7160.5830.6490.417
Test0.7350.5650.6360.411

Per class (test mAP50)

glass0.737biodegradable0.644
metal0.627plastic0.619
cardboard0.594paper0.592

What it means

  • Test ≈ validation → generalises, no overfitting
  • Precision > recall → boxes are usually right, but ≈ 44 % of objects are missed
  • Glass best: clear shape and edges
  • Paper, cardboard worst: few examples, look alike
  • Biodegradable: lowest mAP50-95 (0.330), loose boxes on irregular shapes

Assignment 2 · Task 1

Loss function: triplet loss

Formula

L = max(0, d(a, p) − d(a, n) + m)
  • a anchor, p positive (same class), n negative (other class)
  • d Euclidean distance between embeddings
  • m margin: the negative must be at least m farther than the positive
  • Loss 0 when the gap is already ≥ m → nothing to learn

Why triplet loss

  • Relative goal: same class closer than other class, no fixed distance
  • Varied classes (banana, bread) may stay a bit spread out
  • Look-alikes (paper ↔ cardboard) used as negatives → pushed apart directly
  • Contrastive loss needs fixed distances per pair, harder with varied classes
Assignment 2 · Task 1

Sampling: P × K batches with semi-hard negatives

Our training crops (scaled down, 1 dot ≈ 740 objects)

Batch of 24

What happens

Press 1. Random batch to see what goes wrong without a strategy.
  • P × K: P classes × K crops, here 6 × 4 = 24: every class gets the same share, against the imbalance
  • All look-alike classes meet in every batch
  • Semi-hard negative: further away than the positive, but inside the margin
  • Not the hardest: our labels are noisy, so the hardest may be mislabelled

MetricQuestion
Recall@1is the nearest item the same class?

Q2 · Assigning an unknown sample

  • k-NN vote: the K nearest items vote; the majority class wins
  • Threshold: if even the nearest item is too far → "unknown"
  • New waste types: add a few examples to the gallery, no retraining
